model.name: Localization / Language
model.purpose: Bind language and locale identity, translation and fallback behaviour, terminology constraints and localization quality evidence onto any content-bearing entity of the adopting Dimension, so an agent can determine which language variant exists, how it was produced, how it degrades when absent, and how far it may be trusted.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-031 is a mixin applied to an existing subject entity. Its combined boundary covers three things. (1) Language and locale identity: which BCP 47 tag names a language, script, region or variant, how tags are canonicalised against the IANA Language Subtag Registry, and how locale data inherits toward root. (2) Translation and fallback binding: stable translatable-unit identity independent of source text, source and target revisions, target variant bindings and state, plural and select categories, placeholder and markup contracts, ordered fallback chains, missing-translation policy, terminology concept bindings, and quality, review and rendering evidence. (3) Governance: who owns identifiers and namespaces, who may advance translation state, what access and retention conditions apply to bindings and assertions, and what an agent must read to bootstrap. The mixin binds to documents, message catalogues, translation memories, termbases, media assets and workflow task histories held in their owning systems; it records references, semantic assertions and provenance, and never reproduces their storage format or lifecycle.
in_scope: Language, script, region and variant identity expressed as canonicalised BCP 47 language tags with governed registry provenance
Stable translatable-unit identity that survives source-text change, plus the source revision a translation was made from
Target language variant bindings, variant revisions, staleness against source revision, translation state and approval
Plural and select categories, selector declarations, placeholder and variable contracts, markup and original-code isolation
Declared ordered fallback chains, terminal behaviour, missing-translation policy, and inheritance or override provenance
Terminology concept bindings and term usage constraints referenced into an externally owned termbase
Confidence, quality issue, quality rating, coverage measures, review provenance and pseudo-localization or rendering evidence
Governance of the mixin itself: identifier namespaces, approval authority, access conditions, retention of bindings and assertions
out_of_scope: Storage, format and lifecycle of message catalogues, source documents, translation memories, termbases and binary media assets
Execution of translation workflow tasks, task assignment, vendor purchase orders and task history
Implementation of a formatting or message-selection runtime, and execution of number, date or collation formatting
Machine translation engine training, tuning, decoding and leverage or fuzzy-match scoring algorithms
Character encoding, font selection, text shaping and line-breaking implementation
Runtime evaluation and enforcement of access decisions, and ownership of the audit trail
Execution of erasure or destruction in the owning content, terminology, identity and workflow systems
Statutory language-availability duties, certified or sworn translation attestation, and contractual service-level terms

boundary_notes.neighbor: Content, message-catalogue and asset model of the adopting Dimension
boundary_notes.distinction: The owning system holds the actual source text, catalogue file and media bytes; this mixin holds only the translatable-unit reference, revision pin and digest. XLIFF itself separates the extracted bitext representation from the original format, and ITS External Resource points at, rather than contains, external media that needs localization attention.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Translation management, translation-memory and localization workflow systems
boundary_notes.distinction: Match candidates, leverage scores and task histories are produced and stored by those systems; this mixin records only the resulting binding, its origin and the assertions made about it. XLIFF places translation candidates and change tracking in optional modules carried by the interchange document, not in the subject entity.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Terminology resource governed as a TBX termbase
boundary_notes.distinction: TBX is concept-oriented: a concept entry is language-independent and owns its language and term sections. This mixin references a concept and states a usage constraint for one occurrence; it does not own concept definition, term admission or termbase versioning.

CLDR/LDML supplies plural rules, parent-locale chains and matching data as reference data. This mixin declares which categories a unit requires and which chain applies to it; it does not restate or fork CLDR data, and it does not implement number, date or collation formatting.

WCAG requires programmatically determinable page and part language and equivalent alternatives for non-text and time-based media. This mixin records that a locale-specific alternative is bound and evidenced; conformance evaluation and remediation belong to the accessibility model.

boundary_notes.neighbor: HTTP content negotiation and delivery runtime
boundary_notes.distinction: Content-Language states the languages of a representation and Accept-Language expresses a client preference list; neither is an assertion that a translation exists or was approved. This mixin supplies the binding and fallback declaration the runtime consumes, and does not own negotiation execution or its privacy exposure.

sources.title: Unicode Locale Data Markup Language (LDML) Part 9: Message Format (UTS #35)
sources.relevance: Normative definition of message, pattern, selector, variant key, declaration, external and local variable, placeholder, markup (open, standalone, close), function option and operand type constraints, error classes and required fallback representations, and bidirectional isolation of placeholders.

sources.title: Unicode Locale Data Markup Language (LDML) Part 1: Core (UTS #35)
sources.relevance: Locale inheritance and matching: parent locales, truncation and lateral inheritance, the root locale as terminal fallback, languageAlias canonicalisation of deprecated and macrolanguage subtags, and language matching with match distance.

sources.title: Unicode Locale Data Markup Language (LDML) Part 3: Numbers - Language Plural Rules (UTS #35)
sources.relevance: The six CLDR plural categories (zero, one, two, few, many, other) with other always required, the cardinal versus ordinal distinction, the language-specific nature of the category set, and the plural operands n, i, v, w, f, t, c/e.

sources.title: Internationalization Tag Set (ITS) Version 2.0
sources.relevance: Data categories used throughout this model: Translate, Localization Note (alert/description), Terminology (termInfoRef, termConfidence), Domain, Text Analysis (taClassRef, taIdentRef, taConfidence), Locale Filter (localeFilterList, localeFilterType include/exclude), Provenance (person, org, tool, revPerson, revOrg, revTool, provRef), External Resource, Target Pointer, Id Value, Localization Quality Issue (type, comment, severity, profileRef, enabled), Localization Quality Rating (score, voteScore, profileRef, scoreThreshold), MT Confidence, Allowed Characters, Storage Size.

sources.title: XLIFF Version 2.2. Part 1: Core
sources.organization: OASIS XML Localisation Interchange File Format TC
sources.relevance: Unit and segment structure, unit id uniqueness within the enclosing file, required srcLang and trgLang, translate attribute with inheritance, segment state values initial/translated/reviewed/final with default initial and the constraint that state must be initial when no target exists, subState prefix rule with the reserved xlf prefix, inline codes ph, pc, sc, ec with originalData and dataRef, and note attributes appliesTo, category and priority.

sources.title: XLIFF Version 2.2. Part 2: Extended
sources.organization: OASIS XML Localisation Interchange File Format TC
sources.relevance: Optional modules that show which concerns are separable from the core binding: Translation Candidates (matchQuality, matchSuitability, similarity, origin, type am/mt/icm/idm/tb/tm, ref), Glossary (glossEntry, term, translation, definition, ref, source), Metadata, Validation rules (isPresent, startsWith, endsWith, existsInSource, caseSensitive, occurs), Resource Data, and Size and Length Restriction with sizeRestriction and storageRestriction profiles.

sources.title: RFC 5646: Tags for Identifying Languages (BCP 47)
sources.relevance: Language tag subtag structure (language, extlang, script, region, variant, extension, private use), grandfathered and irregular tags, guidance to use the shortest tag and omit non-distinguishing script subtags, registry stability with Preferred-Value and Deprecated fields for canonicalisation, and the well-formed versus valid conformance classes.

sources.title: RFC 4647: Matching of Language Tags (BCP 47)
sources.relevance: Basic and Extended Filtering, Lookup as selection of the single best match from a language priority list, progressive right-truncation of ranges with single-letter subtags removed together with their trailing subtag, and the requirement that an application MUST define defaulting behaviour when no tag matches.

sources.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
sources.relevance: Content-Language identifies the languages of a representation and explicitly does not identify the language of the intended audience, and may list several languages; Accept-Language expresses a weighted client preference list and a restrictive value is a fingerprinting signal.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
sources.relevance: 3.1.1 Language of Page (A) and 3.1.2 Language of Parts (AA) require programmatically determinable language; 1.1.1 Non-text Content (A) requires an equivalent text alternative; 1.2.2 Captions and 1.2.5 Audio Description require locale-specific non-textual alternatives; 3.1.3 and 3.1.4 (AAA) cover unusual words and abbreviations.

sources.title: TBX Dialects - Introduction to TermBase eXchange (TBX)
sources.relevance: Concept-oriented metamodel conceptEntry to langSec to termSec, the public dialects TBX-Core, TBX-Min and TBX-Basic with the rule that all dialects must comply with the core, and the DCA versus DCT styles. Used only for the concept-oriented structure; the normative text is ISO 30042:2019 and is paywalled.

sources.title: CLDR 36 Release Note
sources.relevance: States that names were added for the pseudo-regions XA (Pseudo-Accents) and XB (Pseudo-Bidi), and that these are intended for testing purposes only and may need special handling to remove them for production.

sources.title: Test your app with pseudolocales
sources.relevance: Scoped implementer evidence for pseudo-localization practice: en-XA adds accents, expands text and brackets each message unit to expose split or concatenated messages and layout breakage; ar-XB reverses direction to expose bidi and mirroring defects; the stated purpose is to find localizability defects before committing text for professional translation.

sources.title: XLIFF Version 2.1
sources.organization: OASIS XML Localisation Interchange File Format TC
sources.relevance: Ratified baseline for the same core constructs used here: unit, segment with aligned source and target, state and subState, srcLang and trgLang, translate, inline codes with canCopy, canDelete and canReorder, note appliesTo and category, and the optional Translation Candidates, Glossary, Metadata, Change Tracking, Validation, Size and Length Restriction and ITS modules.

bundles.name: Translatable Unit and Target Variant Binding
bundles.description: What is identified as translatable, what constrains it on the source side, and how a target language variant is bound to it with a revision, a state and a verifiable reference to the resource that actually holds the text.
bundles.rationale: Every downstream localization assertion is meaningless without a stable subject. XLIFF makes the unit the static container of translatable content with a scoped unique id, and requires srcLang always and trgLang whenever targets exist; ITS Id Value and Target Pointer make the same separation between an identifier, its source node and its target node. Grouping identity, source-side constraints and variant binding into one concern keeps the mixin able to bind without re-hosting the catalogue.

layers.name: Translatable unit identity and source-side constraints
layers.description: The source side of the binding: what the unit is, which source revision is current, what disambiguates its meaning, and what must not be changed or must be limited in any target.

findings.name: Stable translatable-unit identity, source revision and disambiguating context
findings.description: A translatable unit is identified by a key that is independent of the source text it currently carries, scoped to a declared namespace, and paired with the identifier of the source revision a translation was made from, plus the notes that fix its intended meaning, purpose and audience.

questions.text: Which identifier designates this translatable unit independently of its source text, and within which scope is that identifier unique?
answer_data: Unit identifier value issued by the system of record
Declared uniqueness scope such as file, catalogue or product namespace
Identifier issuing authority
Whether the identifier is native to the owning format or assigned by an Id Value rule

questions.text: Which source-text revision is currently in force for this unit, and how is that revision denoted and verified?
answer_data: Source revision identifier
Named digest algorithm and digest value of the source text
Source revision event time and the time this model observed it
Reference to the immediately preceding source revision

questions.text: What context, meaning, purpose or audience notes disambiguate this unit for a translator or an agent?
answer_data: Localization note text with note type alert or description
Domain or subject-matter code
Text-analysis concept or entity reference used for disambiguation
Intended audience and register statement
Where the unit is surfaced, such as button label, error banner or legal notice

questions.text: What must happen to existing bindings when the source text changes while the unit identifier stays the same?
answer_data: Staleness flag raised on each affected target variant
Reference to the source revision each variant was made from
Whether the change is material and requires re-translation or is cosmetic
Grace behaviour while re-translation is outstanding

questions.text: Which content node, message or media element in the owning system does this unit correspond to?
answer_data: Owning system identifier and resource reference
Node pointer or selector expression into the owning representation
Whether the correspondence is one unit to one node or one to many
Segmentation assumption used when a node was split into units

data_elements.name: Translatable unit identifier
data_elements.description: Key that designates the unit independently of its current source text.

data_elements.name: Unit identifier uniqueness scope
data_elements.description: Declared scope within which the unit identifier is guaranteed unique, mirroring the XLIFF rule that unit ids are unique within the enclosing file.

data_elements.name: Source revision reference
data_elements.description: Identifier and digest of the source-text revision that is current for this unit.

data_elements.name: Localization note
data_elements.description: Note to localizers, typed as alert or description, carrying context, meaning, purpose or audience.

data_elements.name: Domain code
data_elements.description: Subject-matter identification of the unit for translation-related applications.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Unit identity, revision pointers and disambiguating notes are inline annotations attached to a subject entity that another system already stores. XLIFF Id Value and unit ids exist inside the owning representation, and ITS Localization Note, Domain and Text Analysis are markup annotations rather than documents. Emitting a separate artifact here would duplicate the owning catalogue and create a second, competing key for the same unit.

findings.name: Translatability scope, protected tokens and target-side limits
findings.description: Which spans are translatable at all, which literals must survive verbatim, which locales the unit applies to, and what character-set and storage-size limits any target text must respect.

questions.text: Is this unit or span marked as translatable, and which rule or inheritance established that value?
answer_data: Translate value yes or no
Whether the value is local or inherited from an ancestor or a global rule
Selector or rule reference that set it
Reason for a no value, such as code sample, identifier or legal citation

questions.text: Which literal tokens, codes or brand strings must appear unchanged in every target variant?
answer_data: Protected token literal and matching mode
Scope over which the protection applies
Whether surrounding whitespace or casing may change
Authority that declared the token protected

questions.text: To which locales does this unit apply, and is that list inclusive or exclusive?
answer_data: Locale filter list of language ranges
Filter type include or exclude
Behaviour for a locale that is neither listed nor excluded
Whether non-applicability means absent, hidden or replaced

questions.text: How is a breach of a protected token, allowed-character set or storage-size limit detected before publication?
answer_data: Allowed characters expression
Storage size value with storage encoding and line-break type
Size restriction or storage restriction profile reference
Validation rule expression such as isPresent, existsInSource or occurs
Verdict, offending span and the agent that produced the verdict

data_elements.name: Translate flag
data_elements.description: Whether the unit or span is intended for translation, with the inheritance source recorded.

data_elements.name: Protected token
data_elements.description: Literal that must be reproduced verbatim in every target variant.

data_elements.name: Locale filter
data_elements.description: Language-range list plus include or exclude type stating the locales for which the unit is applicable.

data_elements.name: Storage or size limit
data_elements.description: Maximum size or length constraint on target text with its encoding and line-break assumptions or its restriction profile.

data_elements.name: Allowed characters expression
data_elements.description: Expression constraining the characters permitted in target text for this unit.

artifacts.name: Protected token and do-not-translate register
artifacts.description: Governed list of literals, code patterns and brand strings that must survive translation unchanged, with the scope, matching mode and declaring authority for each entry. It is the reference set that placeholder and terminology validation consult; it does not contain translations.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Register identified by the adopting Dimension's unit-set namespace; each entry keyed by the literal token plus its declared scope. Keys carry no date component; supersession is expressed by an entry status and a reference to the replacing entry.

layers.name: Target variant binding, revision, state and external resource reference
layers.description: The target side of the binding: which language variant exists, which revision it is, what state it holds, who may advance that state, and where the text or media actually lives.

findings.name: Target variant binding, revision, staleness and translation state
findings.description: A binding pairs one translatable unit with one BCP 47 target language tag and one variant revision, records the source revision it was made from and whether it is now stale, carries the workflow-independent translation state and approval, and separates the time the translation was produced from the time this model observed it.

questions.text: Which canonicalised language tag and variant revision together identify this target variant of the unit?
answer_data: BCP 47 target language tag after Preferred-Value canonicalisation
Whether the tag is well-formed only or validated against the registry
Variant revision identifier and its monotonic sequence
Reference to the unit identifier and its uniqueness scope

questions.text: What translation state does this variant hold, and who is authorised to advance it to the next state?
answer_data: State value from the declared ordered set, for example initial, translated, reviewed, final
Sub-state value with its authority prefix where a local status is needed
Identifier of the role or agent permitted to advance the state
Constraint that the state cannot exceed initial while no target content exists

questions.text: Is this variant stale relative to the current source revision, and by which comparison was that decided?
answer_data: Source revision the variant was produced from
Current source revision
Comparison method such as digest inequality or explicit material-change flag
Staleness verdict and whether the variant remains servable while stale

questions.text: When was this variant produced, reviewed or approved, and when was each of those facts recorded here?
answer_data: Production event time as an RFC 3339 value with seconds and explicit offset
Review and approval event times
Observation or ingestion time recorded by this model
Time zone or offset actually asserted by the producing system

questions.text: Was the target text produced by a machine, by a human, or by a mixed post-editing process?
answer_data: Origin classification machine, human or mixed post-edited
Identifier of the producing tool, person or organisation
Whether the origin was asserted by the producing system or inferred
Whether a machine-produced variant has ever been human-touched

data_elements.name: Target language tag
data_elements.description: Canonicalised BCP 47 tag naming the language, script, region and variant of this target variant.

data_elements.name: Variant revision
data_elements.description: Monotonic revision identifier for the target variant of a unit in one language tag.

data_elements.name: Translation state
data_elements.description: Position of the variant in the declared ordered state set, with an optional prefixed sub-state for locally defined status.

data_elements.name: Staleness flag
data_elements.description: Assertion that the variant was produced from a source revision that is no longer current.

data_elements.name: Production origin class
data_elements.description: Whether the target text is machine, human or mixed post-edited in origin.

data_elements.name: Translation event time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the recorded translation, review or approval event occurred, kept distinct from ingestion time.

artifacts.name: Target variant binding record
artifacts.description: The mixin's own record of one unit-to-language-variant binding: tag, variant revision, source revision pin, state and sub-state, origin class, staleness verdict, and event versus ingestion times. It carries a reference to the target text, not a second copy of the catalogue entry.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by the master-system translatable-unit identifier plus the canonicalised BCP 47 target language tag plus a monotonic variant revision sequence. No date component appears in the key; times are recorded as fields.

findings.name: External resource, catalogue and non-text alternative references
findings.description: Verifiable references from the binding to the systems that actually hold the target text, media asset or alternative, pinned by digest and resolution time, including locale-specific non-text and time-based media alternatives.

questions.text: Which external resource holds the actual target content, and how is it addressed and dereferenced?
answer_data: Owning system identifier and resource reference
Reference scheme and any binding parameters needed to dereference it
Resource kind such as catalogue entry, bitext file, translation-memory entry or media asset
Whether the reference is stable across owning-system migrations

questions.text: What digest or version pin makes the referenced resource verifiable at a stated point in time?
answer_data: Named digest algorithm and digest value
Resource version or revision identifier asserted by the owning system
Resolution time as an RFC 3339 value with seconds and explicit offset
Verification verdict at that resolution time

questions.text: Which non-text or time-based media alternatives must accompany this variant in this locale?
answer_data: Alternative kind such as text alternative, caption track, audio description or transcript
Language tag of each alternative, which may differ from the main variant
Reference to the alternative asset and its owning system
Whether the alternative is required, present, or knowingly absent with a reason

questions.text: What is asserted when the referenced resource is unreachable or its digest no longer matches?
answer_data: Unverified or unresolvable status on the binding
Last successful resolution time and digest
Whether the binding may still be served while unverified
Escalation target within the adopting Dimension

data_elements.name: External resource reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the externally owned resource that holds the target content or asset.

data_elements.name: Resource digest
data_elements.description: Named digest algorithm and value pinning the referenced resource at a stated resolution time.

data_elements.name: Non-text alternative binding
data_elements.description: Reference to a locale-specific text alternative, caption, audio description or transcript required alongside the variant.

data_elements.name: Reference resolution time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the reference was last successfully dereferenced and verified.

artifacts.name: Localization resource reference manifest
artifacts.description: Digest-pinned manifest of every external resource a set of bindings depends on, including catalogue entries, bitext files, media assets and non-text alternatives, with resolution times and verification verdicts. It is a reference index; it never embeds the resource bytes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Manifest keyed by the master-system identifier of the resource set where the owning system issues one; otherwise by a ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension. Each entry is keyed by owning-system resource identifier plus named digest.

bundles.name: Message Form Contract and Fallback Resolution
bundles.description: The formal contract a target variant must satisfy to be substitutable for its source, and the declared, ordered behaviour when no acceptable variant exists.
bundles.rationale: A translation is only interchangeable with its source if it preserves the selection structure and the placeholder set. MessageFormat 2 makes selectors, variant keys, a required catch-all, placeholders, function option types and error fallbacks normative; CLDR fixes the language-specific plural category sets; XLIFF constrains inline codes and their reordering. Separately, RFC 4647 Lookup and LDML parent-locale inheritance both return a value from some other locale when the requested one is absent, which is resolution, not translation. Keeping form and fallback in one bundle prevents that conflation.

layers.name: Selection and placeholder contracts
layers.description: The structural obligations a target variant inherits from its source: which categories it must supply and which variables, placeholders and codes it must reproduce.

findings.name: Plural, ordinal and select categories with selector declarations
findings.description: Which selectors a message declares, in what order they are evaluated, which language-specific plural or ordinal categories the target language requires, and whether a catch-all variant guarantees that every selector value resolves.

questions.text: Which selectors does this message declare, and in what order are they evaluated against variant keys?
answer_data: Ordered list of selector variable names
Function applied to each selector
Variant key list per variant in selector order
Whether the selector value must be a literal rather than resolved from a variable

questions.text: Which plural or select categories must the target variant supply for its own language?
answer_data: Required category set for the target language drawn from zero, one, two, few, many and other
Whether the rule set is cardinal or ordinal
Categories present in the source language that the target does not use
Categories the target requires that the source language never exercises

questions.text: Is a catch-all variant present so that every possible selector value resolves to a pattern?
answer_data: Presence of the catch-all key
Verdict on missing fallback variant as a data model error
Detected variant key mismatch or duplicate declaration
Agent and time of the check

questions.text: Are the categories cardinal plural, ordinal, or an enumerated select set defined by the message author?
answer_data: Selection kind cardinal, ordinal or enumerated select
Enumerated key set and its source of truth where the selection is not plural
Plural operands relied on, such as n, i, v, w, f, t, c or e
Whether the enumerated key set is itself locale dependent

data_elements.name: Selector declaration
data_elements.description: Ordered declaration of the selector variables and functions that rank or exclude variants.

data_elements.name: Required plural category set
data_elements.description: Language-specific set of plural or ordinal categories the target variant must supply, with other always required.

data_elements.name: Catch-all variant presence
data_elements.description: Whether a catch-all variant exists so that every selector value resolves.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Selector declarations and category obligations are properties of the message text itself, which is stored and versioned in the owning catalogue. The category set for a language is reference data supplied by CLDR and must not be forked into a local artifact, because a forked copy silently drifts from the released plural rules. This mixin therefore carries the declaration and the required-category assertion inline against the unit and cites CLDR as the authority.

findings.name: Variables, placeholders, type constraints and code isolation
findings.description: The set of named variables and placeholders the target must reproduce, the value-type and option constraints on each, how original formatting codes and markup are isolated from translatable text, how bidirectional isolation is applied, and what is emitted when a placeholder cannot be resolved.

questions.text: Which named variables and placeholders must appear in the target, and may they be copied, deleted or reordered?
answer_data: Placeholder or variable names present in the source
Whether each is an external or a local variable
canCopy, canDelete and canReorder dispositions for each inline code
Required arity, for example exactly once or at least once

questions.text: What value type, function or option constraints apply to each placeholder?
answer_data: Function applied to the operand
Option names and permitted values
Whether an option value must be set by a literal rather than resolved from a variable
Operand type expectation and the error raised on a bad operand

questions.text: How are original formatting codes and markup kept isolated from the translatable text of this unit?
answer_data: Inline code representation such as standalone, paired, or start and end spanning codes
Original data held outside the translatable text with a data reference
Markup open, standalone or close disposition
Behaviour when a spanning code crosses a segment boundary

questions.text: How is bidirectional isolation applied around placeholders in mixed-direction text?
answer_data: Isolating control characters used around placeholders
Rule that controls are not inserted inside a literal unless part of its value
Base direction assumed for the target language
Whether direction marks inside quoted patterns become part of the output

questions.text: What is emitted when a placeholder or variable cannot be resolved at format time?
answer_data: Fallback representation emitted for the unresolved expression
Error class such as syntax, data model, resolution or message function error
Rule that text, literal and markup resolved values must never be fallback values
Whether the failure is surfaced to the consumer or only logged

data_elements.name: Placeholder or variable name
data_elements.description: Name of a variable or placeholder the target variant must reproduce.

data_elements.name: Placeholder type constraint
data_elements.description: Function, option and operand-type expectation governing a placeholder's resolved value.

data_elements.name: Inline code disposition
data_elements.description: Whether an inline code may be copied, deleted or reordered in the target, and how its original data is referenced.

data_elements.name: Declared base direction
data_elements.description: Base writing direction assumed for the unit's target text, used to decide bidirectional isolation.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The placeholder contract is a derived, per-unit assertion about text that the owning catalogue stores. Materialising it as a standalone artifact would create a second source of truth that can disagree with the message it describes, and the executable form already exists in the catalogue and in the formatting runtime. This model therefore records the contract inline as validation input; XLIFF originalData and MessageFormat placeholders remain owned by their representations.

layers.name: Fallback chain, missing-translation policy and override provenance
layers.description: The declared ordered degradation path when a requested variant does not exist, what happens at the end of it, which layer actually supplied a served value, and how that fact is disclosed.

findings.name: Ordered fallback chain, terminal behaviour and override provenance
findings.description: An explicit ordered list of language tags or locales tried when the requested variant is absent, the mandatory defined behaviour when nothing matches, the record of which chain position supplied a served value and whether that entry was inherited or an override, and the prohibition on presenting a fallback as a translation.

questions.text: What is the ordered list of language tags or locales tried when the requested variant is absent?
answer_data: Ordered chain entries as canonicalised BCP 47 tags
Matching scheme in force, such as basic filtering, extended filtering or lookup
Whether progressive right-truncation of subtags is applied and how single-letter subtags are handled
Whether locale-data parent chains or root inheritance participate, and where they stop

questions.text: What is the terminal behaviour when no entry in the chain matches?
answer_data: Designated default language tag, null result, error condition or implementation-defined default
Which of those the adopting Dimension has explicitly declared
Whether the terminal outcome differs by content class such as legal notice versus label
Consequence for the calling operation

questions.text: Which chain position actually supplied the value served, and was that entry inherited or an override?
answer_data: Index and language tag of the supplying chain entry
Whether the value was inherited from a parent or root, or set as an explicit override at that level
Identifier of the binding that supplied the value
Resolution time as an RFC 3339 value with seconds and explicit offset

questions.text: Is the consumer told that the served text is a fallback rather than a translation into the requested language?
answer_data: Fallback disclosure flag on the resolution result
Actual language of the served representation as declared to the consumer
Whether the requested-versus-served mismatch is machine readable and programmatically determinable
Whether coverage reporting excludes the fallback-served entry

questions.text: Under what conditions is fallback prohibited and an explicit absence or error preferred instead?
answer_data: Content classes for which fallback is forbidden, such as regulated or safety text
Whether a stale or unapproved variant may be served ahead of a fallback
Behaviour when the only candidate is machine output without approval
Declared authority for the prohibition

data_elements.name: Ordered fallback chain
data_elements.description: Explicit ordered list of language tags attempted when the requested variant is absent.

data_elements.name: Terminal fallback behaviour
data_elements.description: Declared behaviour when no chain entry matches, as required by the language-matching specification.

data_elements.name: Served chain position
data_elements.description: Index and language tag of the chain entry that supplied the served value.

data_elements.name: Inherited or override flag
data_elements.description: Whether the supplying entry was inherited from a parent or root, or explicitly overridden at that level.

data_elements.name: Fallback disclosure flag
data_elements.description: Machine-readable assertion that the served value is a fallback and not a translation into the requested language.

artifacts.name: Declared fallback chain profile
artifacts.description: Versioned declaration of the ordered chain, the matching scheme in force, the terminal behaviour, the disclosure obligation and any content classes for which fallback is prohibited. It is the contract a resolver is evaluated against; it does not perform resolution.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Profile name governed by the adopting Dimension plus a monotonic version sequence. The requested language range and content class are evaluation parameters, not part of the key; no date component appears in the key.

bundles.name: Terminology Binding, Quality Assertions and Verification Evidence
bundles.description: What a term occurrence is required to mean, how good a variant is asserted to be, who vouched for it, and what testing shows about whether it actually renders and is usable.
bundles.rationale: ITS separates Terminology from Localization Quality Issue, Localization Quality Rating, MT Confidence and Provenance, and requires MT Confidence to be attributed to an engine through Provenance; XLIFF likewise separates the Glossary module from validation rules. TBX makes the concept, not the string, the unit of terminological identity. Pseudo-locale practice exists because a fully populated locale can still fail to render. Keeping terminology, asserted quality and observed rendering distinct is therefore evidence-led, not stylistic.

layers.name: Terminology and concept binding
layers.description: Binding a term occurrence to a language-independent concept in an externally owned termbase, and stating the usage constraint that applies to it in this locale.

findings.name: Terminology concept binding and term usage constraints
findings.description: Which concept a marked term occurrence denotes, in which termbase that concept lives, which target term is preferred, admitted or deprecated for it in the target locale, how a usage breach is recorded, and what evidence supports an automatic term identification.

questions.text: Which terminology concept does this term occurrence denote, and in which termbase does that concept live?
answer_data: Concept entry identifier or IRI
Termbase system reference and dialect or profile in use
Term information reference resolvable to a definition
Whether the concept is language-independent and which language sections exist

questions.text: Which target term is preferred, admitted or deprecated for that concept in this target locale?
answer_data: Target term string per language section
Administrative status such as preferred, admitted or deprecated
Whether more than one admitted term exists and how to choose
Locale scope of the status, which may be narrower than the language

questions.text: How is a term-usage breach recorded when the approved target term is not used?
answer_data: Quality issue typed as a terminology issue
Severity value and the profile that defines the scale
Offending span and expected term
Whether the breach blocks approval or is advisory

questions.text: What evidence supports a term identification made automatically rather than by a terminologist?
answer_data: Term confidence value on its declared scale
Identifier of the annotating tool, required when confidence is asserted
Whether a human terminologist has confirmed or rejected the identification
Ambiguity note where one surface form maps to several concepts

data_elements.name: Terminology concept reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a language-independent concept entry in the externally owned termbase.

data_elements.name: Term administrative status
data_elements.description: Preferred, admitted or deprecated status of a target term for the bound concept in the target locale.

data_elements.name: Term identification confidence
data_elements.description: Confidence value asserted for an automatically identified term, attributable to the annotating tool.

data_elements.name: Terminology ambiguity note
data_elements.description: Explicit record that a surface form maps to more than one concept and how the ambiguity is resolved or left open.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The termbase owns concept definition, term admission, status governance and its own versioning; TBX makes the concept entry the top-level structure with its own language and term sections. This model carries only the outgoing concept reference, the locale-scoped usage constraint and the confidence or ambiguity assertion for one occurrence. Emitting a local glossary artifact would fork the termbase and let a stale copy override the governed source.

layers.name: Quality assertions, review provenance and rendering verification
layers.description: Asserted quality and coverage, the agents who vouched for it, and the independent observations that show whether the localized product actually renders and is usable.

findings.name: Confidence, quality issue, rating and coverage measures
findings.description: Machine confidence on its declared scale, recorded quality issues with type and severity, any overall rating computed against a named profile and threshold, and coverage measures that state exactly what they count and what they exclude.

questions.text: What confidence value does the producing system assert for this variant, and on which declared scale?
answer_data: Confidence value within its declared range
Scale definition and whether zero to one probability semantics apply
Identifier of the engine or tool the confidence is attributed to
Explicit statement that confidence is a self-report and not an approval

questions.text: Which quality issues were recorded against this variant, of what type and at what severity?
answer_data: Issue type from the declared typology
Severity value on the profile's scale
Comment and the span the issue applies to
Whether the issue is enabled or has been dismissed

questions.text: Against which published quality profile and score threshold was any overall rating computed?
answer_data: Profile reference that defines issue types, severities and weighting
Score and any vote score
Score threshold treated as acceptance
Whether the profile is externally published and versioned

questions.text: What proportion of the unit set has an approved variant in this locale, and how is that proportion defined?
answer_data: Numerator and denominator definitions including which units are in the set
Whether stale variants count as covered
Reference point in time for the measure
Breakdown by translation state

questions.text: Which entries does the coverage measure exclude, and is fallback-served content excluded from it?
answer_data: Exclusion of fallback-served entries
Exclusion of machine-only entries that were never approved
Exclusion of units filtered out for this locale
Statement that coverage does not evidence usability

data_elements.name: Machine confidence value
data_elements.description: Self-reported confidence of the producing engine, on its declared scale and attributed to that engine.

data_elements.name: Quality issue
data_elements.description: Recorded language-oriented quality issue with type, severity, comment, applicable span and enabled status.

data_elements.name: Quality rating
data_elements.description: Overall rating with score, optional vote score, acceptance threshold and the profile reference that defines the computation.

data_elements.name: Coverage measure
data_elements.description: Proportion of the declared unit set holding an approved variant, with explicit numerator, denominator, exclusions and reference time.

artifacts.name: Localization quality assertion record
artifacts.description: Immutable record of one quality assertion about one variant: confidence, issues with type and severity, any rating with its profile and threshold, and coverage measures with their stated exclusions. It asserts; it does not gate publication.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by the variant binding reference plus a monotonic assertion sequence within that binding. A superseding assertion references the prior sequence number; no date component appears in the key.

findings.name: Translation and review agent provenance
findings.description: Which person, organisation or tool produced and which revised the target text, what review occurred and under whose authority it was signed off, where the full workflow history is held, and how attribution personal data is minimised and retained.

questions.text: Which person, organisation or tool produced the target text, and which agent revised it?
answer_data: Producing person, organisation and tool references
Revising person, organisation and tool references
Reference to a shared provenance record where agents are described once
Whether attribution is asserted by the producing system or inferred

questions.text: What review was performed on this variant, and under whose authority was it signed off?
answer_data: Review type such as bilingual revision, monolingual review or in-context review
Identifier of the signing role or agent and its authorisation basis
State transition the sign-off permits
Event time and observation time of the sign-off

questions.text: Where is the full workflow task history held, and what exactly is referenced from here?
answer_data: Owning workflow or translation management system reference
Task or job identifier held there
Which fields this model carries and which it deliberately does not
Statement that this model does not execute or reconstruct workflow

questions.text: What personal data appears in translator and reviewer attribution, and how is it minimised?
answer_data: Categories of personal data present such as name, contact or employer
Availability of a pseudonymous agent reference
Audience permitted to see identified attribution
Lawful basis or policy reference held by the adopting Dimension

questions.text: How long must a review assertion be retained after the variant it describes is superseded?
answer_data: Retention period declared by the adopting Dimension
Trigger that starts the period, such as supersession or withdrawal
What is preserved in a tombstone after disposition
Which system executes the disposition

data_elements.name: Producing agent reference
data_elements.description: Person, organisation or tool credited with producing the target text.

data_elements.name: Revising agent reference
data_elements.description: Person, organisation or tool credited with revising or reviewing the target text.

data_elements.name: Review sign-off assertion
data_elements.description: Assertion that a named review occurred, with review type, signing authority, event time and ingestion time.

data_elements.name: Workflow task reference
data_elements.description: Outgoing reference to the task or job record held by the owning workflow system.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Task histories, change-tracking revision series and vendor job records are produced and owned by the translation management and workflow systems, and XLIFF itself carries change tracking as an optional interchange module rather than as subject data. This model records the minimum attribution and sign-off assertions inline against the binding and points at the owning record. Materialising a local workflow artifact would duplicate an external audit trail this model does not own and cannot keep authoritative.

findings.name: Pseudo-localization and rendering verification evidence
findings.description: Observed evidence that the localized surface actually renders: pseudo-locale runs that expose hardcoded strings, concatenation, expansion and bidi defects, measured fit against declared size limits, the build revision verified, and an explicit statement of what such testing cannot show.

questions.text: Which pseudo-locale runs were executed against this unit set, and what defects did they expose?
answer_data: Pseudo-locale tags exercised, such as the accented-expansion and bidi pseudo-regions
Defect classes observed, such as hardcoded strings, split or concatenated messages, expansion overflow or unmirrored elements
Unit references for each observed defect
Statement that pseudo-locales are test-only and must not reach production

questions.text: Did the rendered target text fit the declared size, storage and layout constraints?
answer_data: Measured rendered length or storage size against the declared limit
Restriction profile used for the measurement
Surface or component in which the measurement was taken
Overflow or truncation verdict

questions.text: Which build or product revision was verified, and when was the run observed?
answer_data: Build or product revision reference
Run event time as an RFC 3339 value with seconds and explicit offset
Ingestion time at which the result was recorded here
Variant revisions in force at run time

questions.text: Which defect classes remain untested by pseudo-localization and rendering checks alone?
answer_data: Semantic and register defects that require human review
Terminology correctness not observable from rendering
Non-text alternative adequacy for captions, audio description and text alternatives
Locale-specific cultural or legal appropriateness

data_elements.name: Pseudo-locale tag
data_elements.description: Test-only locale tag exercised in a localizability run, such as an accented-expansion or bidi pseudo-region tag.

data_elements.name: Rendering defect observation
data_elements.description: Observed localizability or rendering defect with its class, affected unit reference and surface.

data_elements.name: Rendered fit measurement
data_elements.description: Measured rendered size compared against the declared size or storage restriction for the unit.

data_elements.name: Verified build reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the build or product revision the verification run was executed against.

artifacts.name: Localizability and rendering verification report
artifacts.description: Report of one verification run: pseudo-locales exercised, defect observations with unit references, fit measurements against declared restrictions, the build revision verified, and the explicit list of defect classes the run does not cover.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by the unit-set reference plus the pseudo-locale or target language tag plus the verified build revision reference plus a monotonic run sequence. Times are fields; no date component appears in the key.

functions.name: Bind target variant and translation resource
functions.description: Create or update the binding between a translatable unit and one target language variant, pinning the source revision, the variant revision, the origin class and a digest-verified reference to the resource that holds the text.
inputs: Translatable unit identifier and its declared uniqueness scope
Current source revision identifier and digest
Candidate target language tag
External resource reference with named digest algorithm and value
Production origin class and producing agent reference
Translation event time and ingestion time
outputs: Target variant binding record with variant revision and state
Staleness verdict against the current source revision
Digest verification verdict and resolution time
preconditions: The unit identifier resolves within its declared uniqueness scope
The target language tag is well-formed and canonicalised against the language subtag registry
The source revision is known and the target language tag is declared wherever target content exists
The state is initial when no target content is yet present
effects: Creates or supersedes a binding record; existing source revision and origin fields are never rewritten in place
Raises or clears the staleness flag by comparing source revisions
Does not write to, reformat or re-host the referenced catalogue, translation memory or asset

functions.name: Resolve declared fallback chain
functions.description: Given a requested language priority list and the declared fallback chain profile, select the binding that supplies a value, or return the declared terminal outcome, and label the result as translation or fallback.
inputs: Requested language priority list
Declared fallback chain profile version
Index of available bindings with their language tags, states and staleness flags
Content class of the unit where fallback may be prohibited
outputs: Selected binding reference or the declared terminal outcome
Served chain position with its language tag and inherited-or-override flag
Fallback disclosure flag and the actual language of the served representation
preconditions: The chain is explicitly ordered and its matching scheme is declared
Terminal behaviour when nothing matches is declared rather than left implicit
Bindings prohibited from being served, such as unapproved machine output, are identifiable
effects: Emits a resolution result that always distinguishes fallback from translation
Never counts a fallback-served value toward translated coverage
Does not create or alter bindings, and does not perform delivery, negotiation or enforcement

functions.name: Validate placeholder, selection and markup parity
functions.description: Compare a target variant against the source unit's declared selection and placeholder contract, checking placeholder presence and arity, option and operand type constraints, catch-all variant presence, inline code disposition and bidirectional isolation.
inputs: Source placeholder and selector contract for the unit
Target variant text with its inline codes and markup
Required plural or select category set for the target language
Protected token register entries in scope
outputs: Parity findings list with offending spans
Missing, extra or misordered placeholder report
Missing category or missing catch-all verdict
Overall pass or fail verdict with the checking agent and time
preconditions: The placeholder and selector contract is declared for the source unit
Original formatting codes are isolated from translatable text
The required category set for the target language is available as reference data
effects: Records validation findings against the variant binding
Never edits, repairs or reorders target text
Does not by itself change translation state; gating on a failed verdict is performed by the adopting Dimension's runtime

functions.name: Apply terminology constraints to a variant
functions.description: Resolve the concept bindings in scope for a unit, determine the preferred or admitted target term for the target locale, and record compliance or breach findings for the variant.
inputs: Concept references bound to the unit
Target language tag and any narrower locale scope
Target variant text
Termbase reference and the dialect or profile in use
outputs: Term compliance findings with expected and observed terms
Terminology-typed quality issues with severity and profile reference
preconditions: Concept references resolve in the referenced termbase
The termbase declares administrative status for target terms in the relevant language section
A severity profile is named where breaches are scored
effects: Records term compliance findings against the variant binding
Does not create, edit, admit or deprecate concepts or terms in the termbase
Leaves adjudication of an ambiguous concept to the terminologist role

functions.name: Record review and quality assertion
functions.description: Append an immutable assertion about a variant covering machine confidence, quality issues, any overall rating against a named profile and threshold, coverage measures with stated exclusions, and the agents and times involved.
inputs: Variant binding reference
Quality issue list with types, severities and spans
Optional score, vote score, threshold and quality profile reference
Machine confidence value with the engine it is attributed to
Producing, revising and signing agent references
Event time and ingestion time
outputs: Quality assertion record with a monotonic sequence number
Superseded-assertion reference where an earlier assertion is replaced
Coverage measure with explicit numerator, denominator and exclusions
preconditions: Any asserted machine confidence is attributed to an identified engine
Any overall rating names a resolvable quality profile and its threshold
Coverage measures declare whether fallback-served and machine-only entries are excluded
effects: Appends an immutable assertion; prior assertions are superseded by reference, never edited
Does not advance translation state and never converts a confidence value into an approval
Does not own the workflow task history or the audit trail; those remain with the workflow and logging systems of the adopting Dimension

composition.target: Translatable content entity of the adopting Dimension (message, field, document node or media asset)
composition.purpose: Attach translatable-unit identity, target variant bindings, fallback declaration, terminology constraints and quality assertions to a subject that already exists, without becoming the store of that subject's content.

composition.target: BCP 47 language tag identity governed by the IANA Language Subtag Registry
composition.purpose: Take language, script, region and variant identity from the governed registry, including Preferred-Value canonicalisation of deprecated subtags, instead of minting local language codes.

composition.target: Language range matching and lookup behaviour defined by RFC 4647
composition.purpose: Bind the declared fallback chain to a named matching scheme and to the requirement that defaulting behaviour be defined when no tag matches; the algorithm itself is not reimplemented here.

composition.target: Unicode CLDR/LDML locale inheritance, plural rules and language matching reference data
composition.purpose: Cite the released plural category sets, parent-locale chains and root fallback as reference data that constrains what a target variant must supply, without forking or restating that data locally.

composition.target: Unicode MessageFormat 2 message, selector and placeholder model
composition.purpose: Ground the selection and placeholder contract in a normative message model, including catch-all variants, option and operand type constraints and format-time fallback representations; the formatting runtime remains external.

composition.target: OASIS XLIFF bitext interchange documents and their optional modules
composition.purpose: Map unit and segment identity, state and sub-state, inline codes, notes and validation rules to an interchange vocabulary so bindings survive round-tripping through localization tooling.

Adopt named data categories for translatability, notes, terminology, locale filtering, provenance, external resources, quality issues, ratings and MT confidence rather than inventing parallel vocabulary.

composition.target: Terminology resource governed as a TBX termbase
composition.purpose: Carry outgoing concept references and locale-scoped usage constraints while concept definition, term admission and termbase versioning stay with the terminology system.

composition.target: Translation management, translation-memory and localization workflow systems of the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Reference match candidates, job records and task histories held elsewhere; this model records the resulting binding and assertions and does not execute or reconstruct workflow.

composition.target: Accessibility conformance model covering non-text and time-based media alternatives
composition.purpose: Record that locale-specific text alternatives, captions and audio descriptions are bound and evidenced, and that language of page and of parts must be programmatically determinable; conformance evaluation belongs to that model.

composition.target: HTTP content negotiation and Content-Language exposure at the delivery runtime
composition.purpose: Supply the binding and fallback declaration that a negotiating runtime consumes, and require that the served representation's actual language be declared; negotiation execution and its fingerprinting exposure are owned by the runtime.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension MUST name a single owner package for translatable-unit identifiers and publish the scope within which each identifier is unique, mirroring the scoped uniqueness rule the interchange format already imposes.

The owner package MUST declare the authoritative catalogue, translation-memory, termbase, media and workflow systems this mixin references, and MUST NOT re-host their content or fork their versioning.

The owner package MUST publish the ordered fallback chain profile, its matching scheme and its terminal behaviour before any consumer relies on resolution, because the matching specification requires defaulting behaviour to be defined rather than implied.

The owner package MUST designate the approval authority permitted to advance translation state to a published value, and MUST record that this authority is never satisfied by a machine confidence score.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint translatable-unit identifiers only under a namespace the adopting Dimension owns, and never re-key local records by a vendor tool's internal identifier. Express language and locale identity solely as BCP 47 tags canonicalised against the IANA Language Subtag Registry, applying Preferred-Value substitution for deprecated and macrolanguage subtags and omitting script subtags that add no distinguishing value. Keep interchange vocabularies in their own namespaces: XLIFF core and module namespaces, the ITS namespace, and termbase concept identifiers stay qualified and are never flattened into local field names. Pseudo-locale tags are reserved for test scope and must never appear in a production fallback chain.
registry_links: IANA Language Subtag Registry, referenced through BCP 47 for language tag validity, deprecation and Preferred-Value canonicalisation
Unicode CLDR releases, referenced for plural and ordinal category sets, parent-locale chains and language matching data
W3C ITS 2.0 data category definitions, referenced for translatability, provenance, terminology and quality vocabulary
OASIS XLIFF core and module namespaces, referenced for unit, segment, state, inline code and validation vocabulary
Termbase concept identifier space of the adopting Dimension's terminology system

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalise every language tag before comparison or storage: case-normalise subtags, apply registry Preferred-Value substitutions, and omit script subtags that add no distinguishing value; store the canonical form and retain the originally supplied form as provenance.

Store the fallback chain as an explicit ordered list with its matching scheme named; never rely on an implicit truncation order, and record the terminal behaviour as a value rather than as an absence.
Normalise placeholder and variable names to the names declared in the source contract; a target that renames a placeholder is a parity failure, not a canonicalisation task.
Record all times as RFC 3339 values with seconds and an explicit offset, normalising to UTC for comparison while retaining the offset originally asserted by the producing system.

Record digests as a named algorithm plus a lowercase hexadecimal value; apply Unicode normalisation only for text comparison and never treat normalised string equality as evidence of semantic equivalence.
patch_rules: Variant binding records are append-only per variant revision; correcting a target text produces a new variant revision rather than an in-place edit of the previous one.
A change to the source revision MUST create an explicit staleness assertion on every affected binding; silently rebinding an existing variant to a new source revision is prohibited.
Quality and review assertions are immutable once recorded and are superseded only by a later assertion that references the prior sequence number.

Changing a translatable-unit identifier is a create plus deprecate pair with an explicit successor reference; in-place renaming is prohibited because it destroys the identity that survives source-text change.
A fallback chain profile is patched by issuing a new profile version; in-place reordering of a published chain is prohibited.
compatibility_rules: Adding a target language binding, adding a fallback chain entry at the end, adding an optional note, or adding a quality assertion is backward compatible.

Removing or reordering fallback chain entries, changing the terminal behaviour, narrowing a placeholder contract, changing a unit identifier's uniqueness scope, or tightening a size or allowed-character restriction is breaking and requires a new profile or unit-set version.
Deprecated language subtags MUST be retained as recognised aliases mapping to their canonical Preferred-Value form so that historical bindings remain resolvable.
A locally defined sub-state MUST carry its authority prefix so that consumers can ignore statuses they do not understand without misreading them as a core state.
Consumers MUST preserve binding fields they do not understand when rewriting a record, consistent with the interchange requirement to preserve unrecognised defined content.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the subject: the translatable-unit identifier within its declared uniqueness scope, or the owning system's resource identifier for a referenced catalogue entry, asset or job record.

Governed global identifier or IRI: the canonicalised BCP 47 language tag from the IANA Language Subtag Registry for language and locale identity, and the termbase concept identifier or IRI for terminological identity.

UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, used only where no master-system identifier and no governed global identifier exists, and always recorded together with the reason no higher-priority identifier was available.
A date, a revision timestamp, a source-text digest or the source string itself is never an identifier; digests pin content and revisions order it, but neither designates the unit.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All times are RFC 3339 date-time values that include seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z; a time without an offset is rejected rather than assumed to be UTC. Event time and observation or ingestion time are recorded as separate fields whenever they differ: event time is when the translation, review, approval, resolution or verification run actually occurred as asserted by the producing system, while observation or ingestion time is when this model recorded that fact. Neither is derived from the other, and the offset originally asserted by the producing system is retained alongside any UTC-normalised comparison value.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts are named as the artifact identifier followed by a zero-padded monotonic sequence number scoped to one translatable unit and one canonicalised target language tag, for example a variant binding record series per unit and tag. Sequence numbers are never reused and never encode a date; semantic ordering is carried by the referenced source revision, variant revision or build revision, and a superseding item references the sequence number it replaces.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every reference to an externally owned resource carries a named digest algorithm, a digest value and the RFC 3339 resolution time at which verification last succeeded. A binding whose referenced resource is unreachable, or whose digest no longer matches, is marked unverified, MUST NOT be reported as an approved translation, and MUST NOT be counted in coverage. Immutable assertion records are additionally protected by the append-only patch rules, so integrity failure produces a new assertion rather than an edit.

policies: Fallback is not translation. A value obtained through a fallback chain, a parent-locale inheritance step or a format-time fallback representation MUST be labelled as such in the resolution result and MUST NOT be counted as translated coverage or presented as content in the requested language.

Machine output is not approval. A machine confidence value is a self-report attributable to a named engine; however high, it never sets an approved or final state. Only the designated approval authority advances state, and the assertion recording that advance names the acting agent.

String equality is not semantic equivalence. Where source and target text are identical, an explicit assertion MUST be present, such as a do-not-translate flag, a protected token entry, or a recorded human verification, rather than the identity being inferred as either translated or untranslated.

Locale coverage is not usability. Coverage measures MUST state their numerator, denominator and exclusions, MUST exclude fallback-served and never-approved machine entries, and MUST be reported alongside rendering and non-text alternative evidence rather than in place of it.

Referenced catalogues, translation memories, termbases, media assets and workflow task histories remain owned by their systems. This model stores references, bindings and assertions only, and never becomes a second authoritative copy of translated content.

Source-language change, stale translations, ambiguous terminology and missing non-textual alternatives are recorded as explicit, first-class states rather than being resolved by silent fallback or omitted from reporting.

read: A read of a binding MUST return the canonicalised target language tag, variant revision, translation state, origin class, staleness flag and reference verification verdict together; returning target text without its state and staleness is prohibited.
A resolution read MUST expose which fallback chain position supplied the value, whether that entry was inherited or an override, and the fallback disclosure flag.
Coverage reads MUST return the exclusions in force with the measure, so that a figure cannot be quoted without its definition.
Reads of translator and reviewer attribution return pseudonymous agent references unless the caller is authorised for identified attribution.
create: A variant binding may be created only when the translatable-unit identifier, its declared uniqueness scope and the current source revision are all resolvable, and the target language tag is canonicalised.
Creation records both the translation event time and the ingestion time, and records the origin class explicitly rather than defaulting it.
A binding created with no target content is created in the initial state; a higher state at creation is rejected.
A quality assertion may be created only against an existing binding, and any asserted machine confidence must name the engine it is attributed to.
update: Translation state advances only through the declared order and only by the designated approval authority; the acting agent, event time and ingestion time are recorded with every advance.
The source revision reference, the origin class and recorded event times are never updated in place; a correction is a new variant revision or a superseding assertion.
Updating a referenced digest requires a fresh resolution time and produces a new verification verdict, which may set the binding to unverified.
A sub-state may only be set when the core state is explicitly set, and a change to the core state requires the sub-state to be updated or removed.
delete: Deleting a variant binding is a tombstone operation: the translatable-unit identifier, canonicalised target language tag, terminal state, reason and deletion time are retained so that later resolution can distinguish a withdrawn variant from one that never existed. Only the local reference and any locally cached text are removed.

Quality, review and verification assertions are retained for the retention period declared by the adopting Dimension, are never hard-deleted while the variant they describe remains published, and on disposition leave a tombstone recording the assertion identifier, its subject binding and its disposition time.

This model does not own erasure of the underlying message catalogues, translation memories, termbases, media assets or workflow task histories. Deletion there is executed by those owning content, terminology, asset and workflow systems under the adopting Dimension's retention and data-protection policy; this model records only the withdrawal of its reference and the resulting tombstone, and marks affected bindings unverified.

Personal data appearing in translator and reviewer attribution is subject to the adopting Dimension's data-protection policy and is erased by the owning identity system. This model supports a pseudonymous agent reference so that such an erasure does not orphan or invalidate the review assertion that depends on it.
Removal of a fallback chain profile version is prohibited while any recorded resolution result cites it; superseded profile versions are retained as evidence for those results.

roles.name: Localization data owner
responsibilities: Declare the translatable-unit identifier namespace and its uniqueness scope
Publish and version the fallback chain profile, matching scheme and terminal behaviour
Approve breaking changes such as chain reordering, restriction tightening or identifier scope change
Name the authoritative external systems this mixin is permitted to reference

roles.name: Translation approval authority
responsibilities: Advance translation state through the declared order and refuse advancement based on machine confidence alone
Record the acting agent, event time and ingestion time for every state advance
Decide whether a stale variant may continue to be served and under what disclosure
Declare content classes for which fallback is prohibited

roles.name: Terminologist
responsibilities: Maintain outgoing concept bindings and their locale-scoped usage constraints
Adjudicate ambiguous term identifications and record the ambiguity where it remains open
Confirm or reject automatic term identifications carrying a confidence value
Coordinate with the owning termbase rather than forking concept definitions locally

roles.name: Localization quality reviewer
responsibilities: Record quality issues with type, severity and span against a named profile
Record overall ratings only where a resolvable profile and threshold exist
Record review sign-off assertions with the authorising basis
Report coverage measures together with their exclusions and with rendering evidence

roles.name: Integration steward
responsibilities: Maintain digest-pinned references to external catalogues, translation memories, termbases and assets
Re-resolve references and record verification verdicts and resolution times
Mark bindings unverified when a reference is unreachable or a digest no longer matches
Escalate reference breakage caused by owning-system migration or deletion

access.default_rule: Bindings, states, terminology constraints and quality assertions are readable by any agent already authorised for the underlying source content, on the principle that localization metadata is no more sensitive than what it describes. Write access is role-restricted, and translation state advancement is restricted to the designated approval authority. This model declares the required access conditions only; evaluation and enforcement of those conditions are performed by the adopting Dimension's runtime, which owns the decision.
exceptions: Unpublished target variants, embargoed locale launches and pseudo-localization findings MAY be restricted to localization roles ahead of release, while the source unit remains readable.
Identified translator and reviewer attribution MAY be restricted, with pseudonymous agent references exposed to readers outside the localization function.
Quality assertions naming a supplier or engine MAY be restricted where commercial terms require it, without restricting the derived state of the variant.
An embargoed binding MAY be hidden entirely, in which case resolution must behave as if the variant is absent rather than leaking its existence through an error.
audit_requirements: Every translation state advance, digest re-resolution, binding withdrawal and superseding assertion records the acting agent, event time and ingestion time as fields on the record itself.

Access to restricted pre-release variants and to identified attribution is logged, but the log and its retention are produced and owned by the adopting Dimension's logging and audit service; this model only states what must be capturable.
Resolution results that served a fallback record the chain profile version used, so that a later dispute can be reconstructed from declared inputs rather than from runtime behaviour.

read_order: AGENTS.md at the model root, to obtain Name, Type and the four URLs
Specification URL, for the WM-XCT-031 boundary, scope, exclusions and the bundle, layer and finding structure
Storage type URL, for the concrete projection in use, whether document, database or interface-backed, remembering that the projection is not the semantics
Interface URL, for the read, create, update and delete surface and the declared access conditions
Processes URL, for the binding, fallback resolution, placeholder validation, terminology and quality assertion procedures

Referenced registries in this order: the IANA Language Subtag Registry for tag validity, then the current Unicode CLDR release for plural categories and parent-locale data, then the adopting Dimension's termbase

coverage.claim: This model states a defensible context structure for binding translation resources, fallback behaviour, terminology and localization quality evidence onto content in an adopting Dimension, grounded in primary Unicode, W3C, OASIS and IETF material. It claims alignment with those specifications, not conformance to them, and makes no claim of completeness for any specific vendor pipeline, for language-technology quality theory, or for statutory language-availability duty.

checklist.notes: Translatable-unit identity independent of source text with a declared uniqueness scope, target variant identity as canonicalised BCP 47 tag plus variant revision, and terminological identity as a concept reference.
