Identity priority puts the master-system identifier first and explicitly rules out dates, digests and source strings as identifiers.

Translation state with an ordered value set, default initial, prefixed sub-state for local status, staleness against source revision, approval authority, supersession by new variant revision, and tombstoning on withdrawal. Workflow task execution is deliberately excluded and referenced.

Unit to owning content node, unit to variant, variant to external resource and to non-text alternatives, term occurrence to concept, and eleven composition links distinguishing MIX-IN, REFERENCE and ALIGN.

RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset throughout, with production, review, approval, resolution and verification event times kept separate from ingestion time, and source and variant revisions carrying ordering rather than timestamps.

Origin class machine, human or mixed; producing and revising person, organisation and tool references; inherited-versus-override provenance on the served fallback entry; machine confidence attributed to a named engine as the specification requires.

Owner package requirements, five roles, and an explicit boundary that catalogues, translation memories, termbases, assets and workflow histories remain owned by their systems while this model holds references and assertions.

Placeholder and selection parity, catch-all presence, protected token, allowed-character and size or storage restriction checks, term compliance findings, and digest verification verdicts. Gating on a failed verdict is left to the adopting Dimension's runtime.

Default rule tied to authorisation over the underlying source content, four declared scopes, four exceptions covering embargo, attribution, supplier terms and existence-hiding, and an explicit statement that evaluation and enforcement belong to the runtime.

Tombstone rule for withdrawn bindings, retention of assertions while the variant remains published, prohibition on removing a cited chain profile version, pseudonymous agent references so identity erasure does not orphan assertions, and explicit assignment of erasure execution to the owning content, terminology, asset, workflow and identity systems under Dimension policy.

Aligned to BCP 47 and RFC 4647 matching, CLDR plural and inheritance data, MessageFormat 2 selection and placeholders, XLIFF core and modules, ITS data categories, TBX concept orientation and HTTP Content-Language, with unrecognised-field preservation and prefixed sub-states for forward compatibility.
Translatability flags, locale filter include or exclude, selection kind cardinal, ordinal or enumerated, origin class, term administrative status, and quality issue typing against a named profile.

Machine confidence on a declared scale, issue severity against a profile, overall rating with threshold, coverage measures with mandatory exclusions, and rendered-fit measurement against declared restrictions.

Locale-specific text alternatives, captions and audio descriptions are bound and evidenced, and the language of a variant is required to be programmatically determinable. Adequacy assessment and conformance evaluation remain with the accessibility model.

Region subtags in BCP 47 are administrative identifiers used to distinguish language variants, not geographic or jurisdictional claims. No geometry, coordinate or territory semantics are modelled, and none should be inferred from a locale filter.

No primary source consulted supplies a threat model for translation supply-chain tampering, such as malicious injection through a translation memory or a compromised vendor pipeline. Digest pinning and append-only assertions mitigate detection but do not constitute a security model; this is left as an acknowledged gap rather than asserted.

Translator and reviewer attribution is treated as personal data with pseudonymous references, restricted audiences and Dimension-owned lawful basis. The fingerprinting exposure of restrictive language preference is recorded as a runtime concern, not owned here.

known_omissions: Segmentation rules themselves are not modelled; text boundary determination and segmentation-rule exchange were not consulted, so unit-to-node correspondence assumes a segmentation the owning system already performed.
Translation memory leverage and fuzzy-match scoring algorithms are excluded; only the resulting binding and its recorded origin are held.
Grammatical features beyond plural and select, such as grammatical gender and formality dimensions available in locale data, are not given a first-class finding.

The normative text of ISO 30042:2019 for TBX and of ISO 5060:2024 for translation evaluation is paywalled and was not read; terminology structure is taken from first-party companion documentation and quality vocabulary from ITS instead.
Certified, sworn and legally attested translation, and the identity of the attesting authority, are not modelled.
Sign-language variants, Easy-Read and plain-language renditions are treated only as bound alternatives, not as first-class language variants with their own category systems.
Character encoding, font availability, text shaping and line-breaking are excluded, so a variant can pass every check here and still fail to display.
Cost, vendor commercial terms and service-level obligations attached to translation work are excluded.
conflicts: XLIFF 2.1 is the ratified OASIS Standard of 2018 while XLIFF 2.2 Part 1 and Part 2 are Committee Specifications of 2025. The constructs used here are stable across both, but an adopting Dimension should cite 2.1 for conformance claims unless it explicitly accepts a Committee Specification.

ITS 2.0 localization quality vocabulary and the MQM-derived error typology harmonised in ISO 5060 overlap but are not identical, and no crosswalk was verified. Quality records must therefore carry a profile reference rather than assume a shared typology or severity scale.

RFC 4647 Lookup and CLDR/LDML language matching can select different results for the same input, because one truncates a range while the other applies parent-locale data and match distance. A chain declared under one scheme must not be evaluated under the other without restating the scheme.

ITS Locale Filter scopes content by locale while HTTP Content-Language describes the languages of a representation and explicitly does not identify the intended audience. Treating either as an audience or applicability claim overstates what the specifications support.
MessageFormat 2 fallback representations are artefacts of a formatting error, not of locale fallback. Conflating the two hides missing translations behind what looks like a rendered placeholder.

BCP 47 permits both well-formed-only and registry-valid tags; a tag can be well-formed yet not valid. Systems that accept well-formed tags without validation will bind variants under tags that no registry recognises.
regional_assumptions: Region subtags are administrative identifiers for distinguishing language variants; no legal, tax, jurisdictional or geographic inference may be drawn from them.

Plural category sets are language-specific and the required set differs by language; assuming an English one-and-other set for all locales is a defect, and only the other category is universally required.
Right-to-left and bidirectional handling is assumed relevant wherever a right-to-left script appears anywhere in a declared fallback chain, not only in the requested locale.

Statutory or contractual language-availability duties, such as official-language obligations in multilingual jurisdictions, are not modelled here and are owned by the adopting Dimension's compliance model.
Pseudo-locale tags are drawn from user-assigned region code space reserved for testing and are assumed to be filtered out of production configuration by the adopting Dimension.
adversarial_checks: Counterexample sought for the claim that a served string proves a translation exists. Both RFC 4647 Lookup and locale-data inheritance toward root can return a value that originated in a different locale, so a resolved value is evidence of resolution only. This is why the resolution result carries a chain position and a fallback disclosure flag, and why coverage excludes fallback-served entries.

Counterexample sought for the claim that identical source and target text means untranslated. Do-not-translate flags, protected tokens, brand strings and shared technical terms all make legitimate identity common, so identity is treated as requiring an explicit assertion rather than as a defect signal.

Counterexample sought for the claim that high machine confidence implies approvability. The specification treats MT confidence as a self-report that must be attributed to an engine through provenance, which is why confidence is held as a measurement and never as a state transition.

Counterexample sought for the claim that full locale coverage implies a usable product. Pseudo-locale practice exists precisely because fully populated locales still break on expansion, concatenation, hardcoded strings and bidi mirroring, so rendering evidence is kept as a separate finding from coverage.

Structure rejected for lack of primary support: no normative severity scale, weighting or score formula is asserted here, because the consulted specification leaves severity profile-defined and the ISO normative text was not accessible. Only a profile reference and threshold are required.

Structure rejected for lack of primary support: a canonical enumeration of translation origin sub-types beyond machine, human and mixed was not adopted, since the consulted sources enumerate match origins for candidates rather than a governed origin taxonomy for approved variants.

Ownership boundary re-checked against every composition rationale: no bundle, layer, finding or function claims ownership of catalogue or asset storage, translation-memory leverage computation, workflow task execution, formatting-runtime execution, access decision enforcement, negotiation at the delivery runtime, or the audit trail. Each is bound by an outgoing REFERENCE or ALIGN link, and the functions state explicitly that they record assertions and findings without gating, editing or enforcing.
